doom.driver: For the first time, the US military confirms it has deployed weapons in orbit.
doom.summary: The US Air Force has quietly confirmed it has 'on-orbit space control weapons' — which is either reassuring deterrence or the opening chapter of a very bad science fiction novel, depending on your disposition. Meanwhile, AI CEOs are begging Congress to slow down development while Trump calls their concerns a 'hoax,' a tanker just got hit in the Strait of Hormuz, and Treasury yields hit a 19-year peak. It's a day where every threat vector decided to show up at once, like a doom potluck.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: US confirms space weapons in orbit, NATO drones downed over Lithuania, tanker struck in Strait of Hormuz — the map is lighting up on three separate fronts simultaneously.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: The AI industry's own founders are calling for a slowdown, with Anthropic's Jack Clark pushing for mandatory kill switches — which is the technical equivalent of the arsonist asking for a fire extinguisher.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: AI regulation is in full political deadlock: Trump calls safety fears a hoax while Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon agree on exactly one thing — Congress needs to act.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: The AI doomer turn from frontier lab CEOs is notable, but the self-interest angle (slower competitors benefit incumbents) muddies the genuine safety signal.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: 10-year Treasury yield breaching 5% for the first time since 2007 alongside oil squeezes and Fed hike expectations adds a financial stability wildcard to an already crowded threat landscape.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — ground-level view pressed flat against a cracked suburban concrete driveway looking steeply upward at the underside of a backyard satellite dish mounted on a rusted pole, the dish's ribbed concave underside filling the upper frame, deep navy sky beyond it choked with smoldering orange haze, a single bright artificial point of light — too steady, too deliberate to be a star — moving slowly across the narrow band of visible sky between rooftop eaves and dish edge, neighborhood houses flanking both sides reduced to dark silhouetted shapes with curtained windows glowing amber from within, a child's bicycle abandoned on the driveway just entering the lower frame corner, the concrete itself cracked and frost-heaved with dry weeds pushing through, the atmosphere heavy and smoke-filtered, warmth feels threatening, long shadows stretching toward the viewer, the ordinary suburban upward glance suddenly weighted with the knowledge that something overhead has changed forever.

dawn.driver: LSD could be approved for anxiety in the US in 2027. The psychedelic drug LSD eased anxiety in a late-stage trial, paving the way for a probable approval in the US within the next two years
dawn.blurb: SIXTY YEARS LATER, LSD COMES IN FROM THE COLD
dawn.summary: In a week dominated by AI doomers, oil route attacks, and geopolitical friction, a quiet revolution in mental health just cleared its biggest hurdle: LSD passed a late-stage clinical trial for anxiety, putting it on track for US approval by 2027. This is the culmination of decades of stigmatized research finally breaking through regulatory walls — the same substance once banned into oblivion is now being validated by the gold standard of medical evidence. With anxiety disorders affecting hundreds of millions globally, a new approved treatment class could be one of the most consequential medical milestones in a generation.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: A late-stage clinical trial — the rigorous kind — confirmed LSD's efficacy for anxiety, a result that was unthinkable in mainstream medicine just fifteen years ago.

factors.name: Medicine
factors.detail: Regulatory approval by 2027 would make LSD the second psychedelic medicine to enter the US formulary, accelerating the entire psychedelic-assisted therapy pipeline.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Researchers who spent careers working on stigmatized psychedelic science are now watching their life's work become mainstream clinical reality.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: The trial required cross-institutional collaboration between researchers, regulators, and pharmaceutical partners willing to shepherd a Schedule I substance through orthodox approval channels.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A coral reef off Benin, thought dead for 60 years, was found teeming with life — a reminder that systems written off as lost can quietly recover when given the chance.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Interior scene, we are inside a quiet clinical dosing room the morning after, looking outward through a wide doorway into a sunlit corridor beyond, deep golden amber light pouring in from the hallway in long warm shafts across the floor. The room itself is dim and still, lit from the side by a single warm lamp in the corner casting teal shadows along the walls. A soft reclining chair sits empty at the center, a rumpled blanket folded loosely over one arm, an eye mask resting on the seat cushion. On a small side table, a tiny paper cup sits alone beside a printed scoring sheet, numbers descending visibly from high to low in a clean visible arc. The doorway frame is bathed in amber radiance, the corridor beyond glowing with the suggestion of morning and open possibility. Long diagonal shadows stretch across the floor tiles from the door frame. The mood is hushed aftermath, a room that held something momentous now quietly exhaling, the chair the only witness, the blanket still holding the shape of someone who left lighter than they arrived.
